PASS-WITH-NOTES, final C34 round, at 231efbf7e2e2003d5a93657c49d1f0729a6aabf9.

R295-001 closed for the original real sweep/open-before-flock schedule. lock_opened checks the locked descriptor's device/inode against lstat(path). A replaced or missing path returns None and drops the old lock; other metadata errors fail closed. lock_attach performs at most THREE TOTAL opens (at most two reopens), then returns the typed AttachLockHeld/WouldBlock refusal. It cannot spin. Every open retains O_NOFOLLOW, descriptor regular-file/uid/single-link checks before chmod0600. A currently held replacement is still reported as held, not confused with an unrelated EAGAIN. The real-sweep regression and held/dead-holder tests passed.

R295-002 closed for the original live, accepting server after a failed/absent kill-server. remove_server_files retains both files and returns Err until the server-gone probe succeeds; finish_server panics on normal teardown failure and reports on stderr if already unwinding. TestSession and LiveTmuxSession now run their existing teardown assertions before file cleanup. The real accepting-server regression, normal cleanup and panic cleanup all passed.

IMPORTANT qualification, F245 / C34 follow-up P295-R2-001: refusal is NOT proof that every Unix server is dead. In an owned Darwin listener with backlog 1 and one queued connection, a separate blocking connect returned errno 61 (ECONNREFUSED); the SAME listener subsequently accepted and exchanged data, and its socket still existed. Source inference: server_gone and the sweep's refused-connect predicate can misclassify this live full-backlog case. No end-to-end unlink or production apply was performed in this probe. Blocking connect also precedes the loop's deadline, so the stated wait limits iterations only when connect returns.
